subject: Observability: lightweight insight cards linking traces to billing drivers
messages:
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observability: lightweight insight cards linking traces to billing drivers

Team — quick ask. We keep hearing from a couple of enterprise customers (Acme notably) that our per-endpoint insight cards are useful, but they need a much lighter path from a high-level cost spike to two things: a) a playable trace snippet (just the relevant request/response + tokens) and b) a quick decomposition of the top 2-3 billing drivers for that endpoint (model variant, sequence-length buckets, and any cached vs non-cached tokens).

Proposal (minimal, MVP scope):
- Add a small "tracelet" link on the insight card that opens the trace playback focused to the single request (no heavy trace UI).
- Surface a 3-row breakdown: model variant (% cost), token-length bucket (% cost), prefix/cache hit rate (% cost). Each row shows absolute cost delta for the spike window and % of endpoint spend.
- Allow export of the 3-row table as CSV (sample attached).

Why this matters: customers want a one-click explainability path so support & SREs can decide whether to roll back a model variant or change batching/quantization. We need something that is low effort in the Console (no full trace redesign) and can ship in an observability sprint.

I've attached a rough mockup and a sample billing export from Acme. Can you weigh in on level-of-effort + acceptance criteria?

Rishi
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mockup-insight-card.png (PNG, 420KB), billing-sample.csv (CSV, 24KB)
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: lightweight insight cards linking traces to billing drivers

Thanks Rishi — good framing. A couple quick clarifying questions before we scope: 

1) Tracelet: do we need a persisted small playback artifact (like a short JSON snippet stored for 30 days), or can we generate the playback on-demand from traces? On-demand is lower infra cost but may have perf implications for high-retention customers.

2) Billing drivers: the three buckets you listed are clear. Do we want to include a toggle to show token-cost vs wall-cost (customer asks both ways)?

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Insight card shows "Open tracelet" link that opens a focused player with request/response and token timeline.
- Top-3 billing-driver rows computed for the selected window, with percentage contribution and absolute cost delta.
- Export CSV button with same rows.
- Feature gated behind a tenant-level flag for GA.

I can open OBS-907 with these ACs and a rough implementation plan. Tentatively: 2-week design + 3-week backend + 1-week QA if we do on-demand generation. If we persist artifacts (30d TTL), add +2 weeks infra work.

Looping in Marissa/Kim for UX + PM acceptance on the CSV shape and gating plan.

— Priyom
Product Manager, Observability

From: tom.hsu@acme.com (Tom Hsu)
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: lightweight insight cards linking traces to billing drivers

Rishi / Priyom — appreciate you opening this. A few notes from Acme's side: 

- Playback: we do not need full distributed trace context; a single-request playback that shows the prompt, model variant used, tokens, and the first 3 generated tokens is perfect for our tier-one support. If you can persist the snippet for 14 days that would be ideal for audits.
- Billing breakdown: our priority is to see whether a spike was caused by a model switch (we often do nightly variant rollouts), or a sudden uptick of long-sequence traffic (from a new customer flow). The three-row idea is great, but please add a 4th column with an example corrective action (e.g., "rollback variant", "enable caching", "adjust max_tokens").
- Security: we run in private deployment and will need the tracelet to honor tenant KMS and not store plaintext prompts beyond the TTL.

Happy to hop on 30 minutes if it helps.

Thanks — Tom
Senior Ops Lead, Acme Cloud

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observability: lightweight insight cards linking traces to billing drivers

Great — notes captured. Next steps I propose: 

1) Priyom: create OBS-907 with the two implementation variants (on-demand vs persisted tracelet) and cost estimate. Mark persisted artifact as "opt-in tenant" only (14-day TTL, KMS encrypted). Due: Wed 10/13 COB.
2) Kim: small UX mock to add the action column (corrective action suggestions) and CSV column headers. Due: Thu 10/14 EOD.
3) Marissa: coordinate with Acme on a short acceptance prompt set we can use for QA + an export sample contract clause for persistence + TTL. Please confirm legal/security notes for private deployments. Due: Fri 10/15.
4) Rishi (me): I'll present a 10-minute deck to GTM + Solutions on Mon 10/18 to align rollout messaging and tenant flag policy.

I'll update the Jira with owners and link the drive mock. Let's try to keep this scoped to the minimum viable rows and one-click playback so we can test with Acme before expanding.

Thanks team — rishi
